title.narrative: IKI-ALCBT

description.narrative: A call for proposal was floated by Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action (BMWK), Govt. of Germany under International Climate Initiative (IKI) during 2021. Amongst the various themes, “De-carbonization of Building Sector” was one of the priority areas for this proposal. GGGI developed a concept on “798 Low-Carbon Building Transition (ALCBT)” to seek Technical Assistance (TA) from BMKW to implement a Building EE program in 5 798n countries – Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Thailand and Vietnam. The countries were chosen based on a scoping analysis to advance building sector towards decarbonization and reducing GHG emission from the sector.GGGI as a lead, formed consortium with EESL (India), ASEAN Centre for Energy (ACE)-Indonesia and HEAT International (Germany) and submitted the initial proposal to IKI. The consortium partners have their roles as per their credentials and capabilities.This projectseeks to address theregulatory,capacityand financial gaps thatprevent thelarge-scale adoption of energy efficient and low carbon buildings.The interventionsbuildtechnical and institutional capacity for city/state governments to implement policies to achieve national targets for reducing GHG emissions from building operations, particularlyfrom cooling.The interventions aim to transform both existing and new buildings.The project consists of 4 main componentsforenhancing the sustainability of the building sector.While promoting green buildings overall, some projectinterventions focus tospace cooling technologies, as this is increasingly thearea of building energy use in the 798n region.The ALCBT project got formal approval from BMKW on 9th Aug 2023 with effective project start date from 15th Aug 2023.

The overall objective of the project is to create nationwide transition towards low carbon buildings in 798n countries and substantially reducing GHG emissions from the sector with technical, planning, and institutional tools for low carbon buildings that have been successfully implemented by key public and private sector stakeholders in Cambodia, India, Indonesia, Thailand, and Vietnam by 2028, resulting in direct emissions reduction. The 4-dimensional objectives are summarized as below :1. Technical and Institutional Tools : Standardized tools and systems for managing carbon emissions from building sector developed and piloted.2. Technical Capacity Building : Key industry stakeholders in project countries have enhanced capacity to deliver low carbon buildings.3. Financing : Financial pathways established to facilitate financing for occupants, owners, and developers of low carbon buildings.4. Replication and Scaling-up : Project knowledge documented and shared to facilitate replication and scaling up.The project aims to target Policy makers (Central & State Govt), Building Owners, Financial Institutions & ESCOs and Universities/Academia as beneficiary.
